Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better

paper.arxiv.2107.06499

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2107.06499v2. Exact/near duplicate filtering and memorization/attribution caveats establish deduplication workflow; lexical memorization is not a privacy-harm rate. Explicitv2header matches source version. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The analysis did not distinguish harmful from innocuous or desirable memorization and did not evaluate negative effects of deduplication, including loss of attribution or tasks requiring memorization; deduplication alone cannot remove all privacy-sensitive data.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

ExactSubstr uses suffix arrays to remove repeated substrings with a 50-BPE-token threshold; NearDup uses MinHash on 5-grams plus edit similarity greater than 0.8 to identify near-duplicate documents.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The duplication analysis uses the English part of Wiki-40B, LM1B, C4 and RealNews; these corpora had differing prior deduplication procedures, so prior cleaning did not ensure equivalent duplication rates.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

For unprompted top-k sampling with k 50, the authors generated 100, 000 sequences up to 512 tokens and marked tokens within 50-token verbatim training matches as memorized; original-C4 models emitted over 1% memorized tokens, about ten times the deduplicated-model rate.
